attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a plain L3 router (no NAT) between lan-a (node2, eth1) and lan-b (node3, eth1), entirely via an Ansible playbook run from the control node (node4). node2 (10.50.10.10/24) and node3 (10.50.20.10/24) route through node1 (10.50.10.254 / 10.50.20.254) and reach each other directly on any port with original source addresses preserved (verified via tcpdump showing an unmodified source IP through a full TCP handshake). All four managed nodes were then restarted one at a time via their native reboot mechanisms; each showed a changed boot_id and fully recovered state (VyOS committed config persisted via `save`; Alpine static IP/route persisted via /etc/network/interfaces; a full re-run of the playbook after all restarts was 100% idempotent with connectivity re-confirmed).
